tasks.title: Literal and length
tasks.statement:
Declare s = "Привет, мир!" and print two lines: the string itself, then «bytes=…» and «chars=…» on one line: «bytes=21 chars=12».

Expected output:
«Привет, мир!
bytes=21 chars=12»
tasks.hint: len() is bytes, chars().count() is characters.

tasks.title: Building a String
tasks.statement:
Create an empty mutable String, append push_str("Rust"), push(' '), push_str("любит"), push(' '), push_str("тебя") and print «Rust любит тебя».

Expected output:
«Rust любит тебя»
tasks.hint: push takes a character in single quotes, push_str takes a string.

tasks.title: Concatenating with plus
tasks.statement:
Join the String a = «раз» and the &str «два» with the + operator, then add «три» and print «раздватри». The left operand of plus is a String.

Expected output:
«раздватри»
tasks.hint: String on the left, &str on the right.

tasks.title: format!
tasks.statement:
name = "Аня", age = 30. Using format!, build in a variable the string «Аня, 30 лет» and print it.

Expected output:
«Аня, 30 лет»
tasks.hint: format!("{}, {} лет", name, age)

tasks.title: join
tasks.statement:
Join the words ["сыр", "хлеб", "молоко"] with the join method and the separator ", " and print «сыр, хлеб, молоко».

Expected output:
«сыр, хлеб, молоко»
tasks.hint: words.join(", ")

tasks.title: Repeating
tasks.statement:
Using the repeat method, print a line of 20 dashes «--------------------», then «Rust», and 20 dashes again.

Expected output:
--------------------
Rust
--------------------
tasks.hint: "-".repeat(20)

tasks.title: Letter case
tasks.statement:
s = "Привет, Мир". Print s.to_uppercase() and s.to_lowercase() — two lines: «ПРИВЕТ, МИР» and «привет, мир».

Expected output:
«ПРИВЕТ, МИР
привет, мир»
tasks.hint: The methods return a new string.

tasks.title: trim and replace
tasks.statement:
s = "   много   пробелов   ". Print the trimmed string, and then replace("много", "мало") on the trimmed string: «много   пробелов» and «мало   пробелов».

Expected output:
«много   пробелов
мало   пробелов»
tasks.hint: trim removes spaces only at the edges.

tasks.title: Searching for a substring
tasks.statement:
text = "Rust — язык системного программирования". Print three lines: contains("язык"), starts_with("Rust"), ends_with("Go") → true, true, false.

Expected output:
true
true
false
tasks.hint: The result of each method is a bool.

tasks.title: find
tasks.statement:
text = "hello world". Print the position of the first occurrence of «o» (find returns an Option, so add unwrap) and the position of «wor»: «4» and «6».

Expected output:
4
6
tasks.hint: find returns Option<usize>; unwrap takes the value out.

tasks.title: Looping over characters
tasks.statement:
For the string "раст" print each character on its own line with a for loop over chars().

Expected output:
«р
а
с
т»
tasks.hint: for c in "раст".chars() { … }

tasks.title: Vowels
tasks.statement:
In the string "Программирование на Rust" count the Russian vowels «аеёиоуыэюя» (case does not matter: convert to lowercase first). Print «8».

Expected output:
8
tasks.hint: "…".contains(c) can search for a character.

tasks.title: Reversing a string
tasks.statement:
Reverse the string "привет" with chars().rev().collect::<String>() and print «тевирп».

Expected output:
«тевирп»
tasks.hint: chars().rev() and collect into a String.

tasks.title: Palindrome
tasks.statement:
Check whether «А роза упала на лапу Азора» is a palindrome, ignoring spaces and case. Print «true».

Expected output:
true
tasks.hint: Remove the spaces, convert to lowercase, compare with the reversed string.

tasks.title: Word count
tasks.statement:
Count the words in the string "  раз  два   три четыре " with split_whitespace().count(): «4».

Expected output:
4
tasks.hint: split_whitespace ignores extra spaces.

tasks.title: Sum of numbers from a string
tasks.statement:
From the string "10, 20, 30, 5" extract the numbers (split on the comma, trim, parse::<i32>) and print the sum «65».

Expected output:
65
tasks.hint: part.trim().parse::<i32>().unwrap()

tasks.title: Lines of text
tasks.statement:
text = "раз\nдва\nтри". Print each line with its number in the format «1: раз», «2: два», «3: три» (lines and enumerate).

Expected output:
«1: раз
2: два
3: три»
tasks.hint: enumerate gives (index, value) pairs; the index starts from zero.

tasks.title: String slice
tasks.statement:
text = "Hello, Rust!". Print the slices &text[0..5], &text[7..11] and &text[7..] — «Hello», «Rust» and «Rust!».

Expected output:
Hello
Rust
Rust!
tasks.hint: For an ASCII string, bytes and characters coincide.

tasks.title: The n-th character
tasks.statement:
s = "привет". Print the third character (index 2, via chars().nth(2)) and the last one (chars().last()). The expected output is «и» and «т». Both are Options, use unwrap.

Expected output:
«и
т»
tasks.hint: nth(n) returns Option<char>.

tasks.title: Character positions
tasks.statement:
For the string "аб" print «position character» pairs with char_indices: «0 а» and «2 б» (a Russian letter is 2 bytes).

Expected output:
«0 а
2 б»
tasks.hint: char_indices gives the offset in bytes.

tasks.title: Alignment
tasks.statement:
Print three lines: the number 42 right-aligned in a field of width 8 («[      42]»), the word «Rust» left-aligned in a field of 8 («[Rust    ]») and «hi» centered in a field of 8 with the fill character «*» («[***hi***]»).

Expected output:
[      42]
[Rust    ]
[***hi***]

tasks.title: Precision of a float
tasks.statement:
x = 3.14159265. Print x with 0, 2 and 4 digits after the decimal point — «3», «3.14», «3.1416» (one per line).

Expected output:
3
3.14
3.1416

tasks.title: Leading zeros
tasks.statement:
Print the number 7 as «007» (field width 3, zeros on the left: {:03}), and 255 in hexadecimal, zero-padded to a field of 4 with the prefix 0x: «0x00ff» (format {:#06x}).

Expected output:
007
0x00ff

tasks.title: Debug format
tasks.statement:
Print the string "привет\n" through {:?} (in quotes and with escaping: «"привет\n"») and the tuple (1, "a", 2.5) through {:?}: «(1, "a", 2.5)».

Expected output:
«"привет\n"»
(1, "a", 2.5)
tasks.hint: {:?} is the debug representation.

tasks.title: Comparing strings
tasks.statement:
Print: «apple» < «banana» (true), «Zebra» < «apple» (true, capitals come first) and String::from("abc") == "abc" (true).

Expected output:
true
true
true
tasks.hint: Strings are compared by bytes.

tasks.title: Shout
tasks.statement: Write a function shout(s: &str) -> String: the string in uppercase with three exclamation marks at the end.
tasks.hint: format!("{}!!!", s.to_uppercase())

tasks.title: How many times it occurs
tasks.statement: Write a function count_char(s: &str, ch: char) -> usize: how many times the character ch occurs in s.
tasks.hint: A loop over chars and a counter.

tasks.title: The first word
tasks.statement: Write a function first_word(s: &str) -> &str: the first word of the string (up to the first space; if there are no spaces, the whole string).
tasks.hint: find(' ') returns the position of the space; the slice is &s[..i].

tasks.title: Capitalize the first letter
tasks.statement: Write a function capitalize(s: &str) -> String: the first letter in uppercase, the rest unchanged (an empty string stays empty).
tasks.hint: chars().next() gives the first letter, the rest is chars.as_str().

tasks.title: Caesar cipher
tasks.statement: Write a function caesar(s: &str, shift: u8) -> String for the Latin letters a–z: shift each lowercase letter forward by shift, wrapping around (z → a), and leave all other characters unchanged.
tasks.hint: The letter's number is c as u8 - b'a'; shift modulo 26; add b'a' to go back.
